title: Best Golf Cart Pickup Truck: Your Complete Guide
metaDescription: Discover the best golf cart pickup truck options. Learn about types, buying tips, and how to transport your golf cart safely.
content:
If you own a golf cart, you've probably wondered about the best way to transport it. A golf cart pickup truck is more than just a vehicle—it's a solution for hauling your cart to the course, around the property, or to a new location. Whether you're looking for a truck that can carry a golf cart in its bed or a dedicated carrier, this guide covers everything you need to know.

## Why You Need a Golf Cart Pickup Truck

A golf cart pickup truck offers versatility. Instead of relying on a trailer, you can load the cart directly into the truck bed. This saves time and makes maneuvering easier. Plus, many trucks are designed for off-road use, making them perfect for golf courses or large estates. The combination of a truck and golf cart is ideal for maintenance, security patrols, or simply getting around in style.

## Types of Golf Cart Pickup Trucks

Not all trucks are created equal when it comes to hauling a golf cart. Here are the main categories:

### Full-Size Pickup Trucks
Full-size trucks like the Ford F-150 or Ram 1500 have long beds that can accommodate most golf carts. With a truck body for golf cart modifications, you can even customize the bed to secure the cart. These trucks offer high towing capacity if you prefer a trailer.

### Compact Pickup Trucks
Smaller trucks like the Toyota Tacoma or Ford Ranger are lighter and easier to park. However, a golf cart in a 6.5 truck bed may require careful measuring. Some compact trucks have shorter beds, so you might need a golf cart carrier for the truck or a rack system.

### Custom Golf Cart Trucks
Some manufacturers produce dedicated truck golf cart hybrids. These vehicles have a truck-like bed but are built on a golf cart chassis. They're perfect for light hauling on flat terrain. Think of them as a golf cart semi truck—but smaller and more nimble.

## What to Consider Before Buying a Golf Cart Pickup Truck

Before you purchase, think about these factors:

### Bed Length and Capacity
Measure your golf cart. A standard golf cart is about 8 feet long. A 6.5-foot bed won't fit the cart without the tailgate down. If you want the golf cart in the back of a truck securely, consider an 8-foot bed or a bed extender. Also check payload capacity—most carts weigh 500-1000 lbs, so ensure your truck can handle that plus passengers.

### Loading Method
How will you get the golf cart into the bed? Ramps are the most common. Look for trucks with a low bed height or add a lift kit. Some people use a truck bed golf cart carrier that slides out. For heavy carts, a powered winch helps.

### Purpose and Terrain
Will you drive the truck and golf cart on roads, grass, or rough terrain? A truck with four-wheel drive is better for muddy courses. If you need a golf cart tow truck, consider the truck's towing capacity for a trailer.

### Legal Requirements
Check local laws. Some areas require the golf cart to be tied down and have working lights if transported on public roads. A truck body for golf cart might need special registration.

## How to Load and Transport Your Golf Cart

Loading a golf cart in truck bed requires care. Follow these steps:

1. Use sturdy ramps rated for the cart's weight.
2. Drive the cart slowly up the ramps. Have a spotter guide you.
3. Center the cart over the axle for balanced weight.
4. Secure with ratchet straps—attach to the truck's tie-down points and the cart's frame. Never strap to the roof or plastic parts.
5. If the tailgate is down, use a bed extender to support the cart's overhang.

For a golf cart in the back of a truck, always double-check that the straps are tight and the cart won't shift during turns or braking.

## FAQs

### Can a golf cart fit in a standard truck bed?

Most golf carts are about 8 feet long, so they won't fit fully inside a standard 5.5- or 6.5-foot bed. You'll need an 8-foot bed or a bed extender. Alternatively, use a trailer. Always measure your cart and truck bed before attempting.

### What is the best way to secure a golf cart in a truck bed?

Use high-quality ratchet straps attached to the truck's anchor points. Cross the straps over the cart's frame to prevent side-to-side movement. Also, tie down the front and rear. Avoid using bungee cords—they can stretch and loosen.

### Do I need a special trailer to haul a golf cart?

Not necessarily. Many people transport golf carts in the bed of a truck or on a standard utility trailer. However, if your truck bed is too short, a dedicated golf cart trailer with low ramps is easier. Ensure the trailer is rated for the cart's weight.

---

Choosing the right golf cart pickup truck depends on your needs. Whether you opt for a full-size truck with a long bed or a compact model with a carrier, safety and fit should be your top priorities. By considering bed size, loading method, and legal requirements, you'll find the perfect setup for your golf cart adventures.

title: Best Golf Practice in House: Transform Your Home Into a Driving Range
metaDescription: Discover the best golf practice in house with our guide. Learn about gear, setup, and tips for effective indoor home golf practice.
content:
Improving your golf game doesn't always require a trip to the course. With the right setup and equipment, golf practice in house can be just as effective. Whether you're looking to refine your swing, work on putting, or simply stay sharp during off-season, creating a dedicated practice area at home is easier than you think.

## Why Practice Golf at Home?

Consistency is key in golf. By practicing golf at home, you remove barriers like travel time, weather, and course fees. You can get in quality repetitions whenever you have a few minutes. In home golf practice allows you to focus on specific aspects of your game without distractions. Plus, it's a great way to involve family or friends in a fun activity.

## Choosing the Right Space for Indoor Golf Practice

Before buying any golf practice equipment, assess your available space. For indoor home golf practice, you'll need enough room to make a full swing safely. Measure ceiling height—at least 8-10 feet is ideal. Also, consider the floor surface; carpet or a golf mat can protect your flooring and simulate turf. If space is tight, focus on putting and chipping drills that require less room.

## Essential Equipment for Golf Practice at Home

### Golf Mats
A high-quality golf mat is the foundation of any home golf practice setup. Look for a mat that mimics real turf and can withstand repeated swings. Many mats have a rubber base to prevent slipping and a grass-like surface that allows a real divot feel.

### Practice Balls
Not all balls are created equal for indoor use. Practice golf balls at home often include foam or plastic versions that reduce the risk of damage. Some are designed to fly only short distances, making them perfect for swing practice in confined spaces. For full-swing practice, consider net setups with limited-flight balls.

### Golf Nets
A golf net is essential for capturing balls after impact. Choose a net that is durable and large enough to catch mishits. Some nets come with a target screen to improve accuracy.

### Putting Greens
Indoor putting mats can range from simple straight strips to undulating greens with multiple holes. Practicing golf indoors is great for honing putting stroke and reading breaks.

## What to Consider Before Buying Golf Practice Gear

When shopping for golf practice in house equipment, keep these factors in mind:

- **Space constraints**: Measure your area before buying. A full-swing net requires more room than a putting mat.
- **Safety**: Ensure the net is secure and that breakable items are moved. Also, consider the noise—some mats and balls are quieter than others.
- **Portability**: If you need to set up and take down frequently, look for lightweight, foldable options.
- **Durability**: Read reviews about mat and net wear. Some cheaper mats may not last.
- **Budget**: Quality varies widely. You don't need the most expensive gear to practice effectively, but avoid the cheapest that may break quickly.

## Tips for Effective Home Golf Practice

To get the most out of your home golf practice setup:

1. **Create a routine** – Warm up with stretches, then work through swings with different clubs.
2. **Use video analysis** – Record your swing to identify flaws.
3. **Focus on fundamentals** – Grip, stance, and alignment are easier to check at home.
4. **Mix full swings with short game** – hitting only long shots can neglect scoring areas.
5. **Set goals** – For example, make 10 consecutive putts from 3 feet before moving on.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much space do I need for indoor golf practice?
At minimum, you need a clear area about 8-10 feet wide, 8-10 feet tall, and 10-12 feet deep for a full swing. For putting only, a smaller area of 6x10 feet can work.

### Can I practice golf in an apartment?
Yes, with the right equipment. Use foam practice balls, a quiet mat, and a net that absorbs impact. Check with your building about noise restrictions. Many apartment dwellers successfully practice putting and chipping indoors.

### Do I need expensive gear to practice golf at home?
No. You can start with a simple putting mat and a few foam balls. As you improve, you can invest in a mat, net, and accessories. Many golfers see significant improvement with budget-friendly setups.

## Final Thoughts

Golf practice in house is a smart investment in your game. With the right space and equipment, you can practice effectively regardless of weather or schedule. Focus on the fundamentals, stay consistent, and enjoy the convenience of home practice. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned player, at-home practice will help you lower your scores.

Remember, the best golf practice at home is the practice you actually do. Set up your space today and start improving tomorrow.

## Understanding Your Harley Davidson Golf Cart Model

Before buying any parts, you need to know exactly what you’re working with. Harley Davidson produced golf carts under the AMF brand from the 1960s through the early 1980s. The most common years include 1969, 1970, 1974, 1976, and 1980. Later models (after 1982) were sold as Columbia ParCar, but many parts remain interchangeable. Look for a serial number tag on the frame or under the seat to identify the year and model. Vintage golf cart parts harley davidson are model-specific, so matching the year is critical.

## Essential Harley Davidson Golf Cart Parts to Know

### Engine Parts
Harley davidson golf cart engine parts are among the most requested. These carts used two-stroke engines (typically 250cc or 300cc) in earlier models, and later switched to four-stroke. Common needs include pistons, rings, carburetors, ignition coils, and exhaust systems. For used harley davidson golf cart parts, engine components are often available from restorers.

### Body and Frame Parts
Body panels, seats, windshields, and trim are frequently damaged or missing. Fiberglass body parts can be repaired, but replacements are scarce. Look for vintage harley davidson golf cart parts from salvage yards or online forums. Floor pans and dashboard pieces are also popular.

### Electrical and Drivetrain
Solenoids, voltage regulators, wiring harnesses, and switches fail over time. The parts diagram can help you trace circuits. Axles, differentials, and clutches are also common wear items. If you’re restoring a 1976 harley davidson golf cart, you’ll want to check the brake cables and cables as they often rust.

## What to Consider Before Buying Harley Davidson Golf Cart Parts

- **Condition**: Used parts may have hidden wear. For mechanical parts, consider rebuilding rather than buying unknown used. For cosmetic parts, surface rust or cracks can often be repaired.

- **Budget**: Engine parts are typically the most costly. Set a budget before starting a restoration. You can find harley davidson amf golf cart parts at reasonable prices if you hunt.

You can search for “harley davidson amf golf cart” or “1970 harley davidson golf cart” to narrow results. Specialized golf cart forums and Facebook groups often have members selling parts. Some companies still produce reproduction parts for popular models like the 1969 harley davidson golf cart. Golf cart salvage yards may have entire carts for parting out. If you need a part diagram, many are available in PDF form from enthusiast sites.

Look for the AMF logo on the front emblem or serial number plate. If the cart was built between 1966 and 1982, it’s likely an AMF Harley-Davidson. The serial number can also be cross-referenced online.

title: Titleist NXT Golf Balls: Discontinued in 2018. What They Were and What Replaced Them
metaDescription: Titleist replaced the NXT Tour and NXT Tour S with the Tour Soft in 2018. What the NXT balls were, whether old or recycled NXTs are worth playing, and the current Titleist equivalents.
content:
Titleist **discontinued the NXT line in 2018**. The **NXT Tour** and **NXT Tour S** were replaced by one ball, the **Tour Soft**, launched at **$35 a dozen**. Any NXTs you find now are old stock or recycled. Fine for practice, but you can't keep buying the same ball.

## What the NXT balls were

The NXT family sat below the Pro V1 and Pro V1x: a cheaper option for golfers who wanted Titleist quality without tour-ball spin or price.

- **NXT Tour:** the firmer of the two, aimed at distance with decent greenside control.
- **NXT Tour S:** the "S" stood for soft. It was a lower-compression version for golfers who prioritised feel, and it was also sold in yellow.

When Titleist retired them, it said its research showed golfers in this category mostly cared about two things, distance and feel, rather than construction details, so it replaced both NXTs with a single ball.

## What replaced them

| If you played… | Current Titleist option | Why |
|---|---|---|
| NXT Tour S (soft feel) | **Tour Soft** | Built around a very large 1.60-inch core and soft ionomer-blend cover for feel and distance |
| NXT Tour (distance) | **Tour Soft** or **Velocity** | Velocity is Titleist's distance-first ball. The 2018 version had a lower-compression core and came in several colours |
| NXT, but you want more short-game spin | **Pro V1 / AVX** | Urethane covers for more greenside spin, at a higher price |

## Are old or recycled NXTs worth it?

For **practice, scrambles and casual rounds**, good-condition recycled NXTs are a cheap way to play a decent ball. Keep in mind:

- They're at least **eight years old**. Stored badly, any ball loses some of its pop.
- Choose **"mint" or top-grade** recycled balls, and avoid scuffs and cuts.
- **Mixed batches play differently.** Tour and Tour S feel noticeably different.

For a ball you'll play every round, pick a current model you can buy again. Our [soft-feel golf balls guide](/shop/best-soft-feel-golf-balls) and [guide to old golf balls](/shop/best-old-golf-balls) can help.

faq.answer: No. Titleist discontinued the NXT Tour and NXT Tour S in 2018 and replaced both with a single ball, the Tour Soft.

faq.answer: The Titleist Tour Soft, launched in 2018 at $35 a dozen, with a very large 1.60-inch core and an ionomer-blend cover aimed at soft feel and distance.

faq.answer: For practice and casual rounds, yes if they're in good condition, but they are now several years old at best. For a consistent ball you can buy again and again, choose a current model.

title: Best Golf Launch Monitors by Budget: Radar vs Camera, Space and Subscriptions
metaDescription: Golf launch monitors compared from ~$500 to $15,000+: Garmin R10, Rapsodo MLM2PRO, Square, Mevo, Bushnell Launch Pro, Uneekor, Foresight GC3, Garmin R50 and more, with space needs and subscription costs.
content:
The right launch monitor depends on **two things: your budget and how deep your room is.** Roughly:

- **Under ~$1,000:** radar or hybrid units such as the **Garmin R10**, **Rapsodo MLM2PRO** or **Square Golf**. Great for practice and casual sim golf.
- **~$1,000–$3,000:** the **FlightScope Mevo** range, **Bushnell Launch Pro** and **Uneekor EYE MINI**. Much better indoor spin and club data.
- **$5,000+:** **Garmin R50**, **Full Swing KIT**, **Foresight GC3/GCQuad**, **Uneekor EYE XO2**, **TrackMan**. Near-tour data and premium simulator software.

**Camera units that sit beside the ball suit short rooms. Radar units that sit behind you need more depth.** Check your space with our [simulator room calculator](/shop/golf-simulator-room-size) first.

## Comparison at a glance

| Model | Approx. price* | Technology | Sits | Room depth needed | Subscription for full sim use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Garmin Approach R10 | ~$500–$600 | Radar | Behind ball | ~14–16 ft | ~$99/yr |
| Rapsodo MLM2PRO | ~$700 | Radar + cameras | Behind ball | ~14–16 ft | Yes (e.g. ~$250/yr for GSPro) |
| Square Golf | ~$700 | Cameras | Beside ball | ~10–12 ft | Yes (e.g. ~$250/yr GSPro) |
| FlightScope Mevo / Mevo+ range | ~$1,100–$1,300 | 3D radar + camera | Behind ball (7–9 ft back) | 16 ft+ | Varies by model |
| Bushnell Launch Pro | ~$3,000 | 3 cameras | Beside ball | ~10–12 ft | ~$199–$599/yr tiers |
| Uneekor EYE MINI | ~$3,000 | Cameras (IR) | Beside ball | ~10–12 ft | Third-party software |
| Garmin Approach R50 | ~$5,000 | 3 cameras + built-in screen | Beside ball | ~10–12 ft | Included |
| Full Swing KIT | ~$5,000 | Radar | Behind ball | ~14–16 ft | Third-party software |
| Foresight GC3 | ~$7,000 | 3 cameras | Beside ball | ~10–12 ft | Basic free; courses extra |
| Uneekor EYE XO2 | ~$11,000 | Overhead cameras | Ceiling | ~12 ft ceiling | Yes |
| Foresight GCQuad | ~$16,000–$18,000 | 4 cameras | Beside ball | ~10–12 ft | Foresight software |
| TrackMan iO | ~$14,000+ | Ceiling radar + cameras | Ceiling | Pro install | Included |

*Prices are list or typical street prices at the time of writing, from the source below. They change often, so check before buying.

## Radar vs camera, in plain terms

**Radar (Doppler)** tracks the ball in flight. Outdoors, with room to fly, it's excellent. Indoors the ball only travels 10–12 ft before the screen, so the unit needs space behind you to see enough of the flight. Some budget units estimate spin, or need special marked balls to measure it.

**Camera (photometric)** units photograph the ball, and often the club, in the first few inches after impact. They work in shorter rooms and measure spin directly, which is why they're the default for serious indoor setups. The trade-off is price, and you need decent lighting around the hitting area.

**Overhead/ceiling** systems (Uneekor EYE XO2, TrackMan iO) keep the floor clear and work for left- and right-handers without moving anything. They need enough ceiling height and a fixed installation.

## The real cost: hardware + software + room

Many monitors need a **subscription** for full simulator play, course libraries or club data: typically **$100–$600 a year**. Add it up over five years before comparing two units on price. Then budget for the rest of the setup: screen, enclosure, mat and projector. Our [golf simulator cost guide](/shop/golf-simulator-cost) breaks it down.

## Which one should you buy?

- **Practice-focused, tight budget, garage with depth:** Garmin R10 or Rapsodo MLM2PRO. See our [launch monitors under $500](/shop/best-budget-golf-launch-monitor-under-500) for the cheapest options.
- **Short room (basement, spare room) and serious about data:** a side-of-ball camera unit such as the Bushnell Launch Pro or Uneekor EYE MINI.
- **Dedicated sim room, mixed left- and right-handers:** consider an overhead system.
- **"Buy once" premium:** Foresight GC3 or GCQuad, Garmin R50 (built-in display) or TrackMan.

Whatever you choose, **the launch monitor is the part to spend on first**. A great screen in front of an inaccurate monitor is still an inaccurate simulator. Our [simulator buying guide](/shop/best-golf-sim-buying-guide) puts all the pieces together.

Under about $1,000, radar units such as the Garmin R10 or Rapsodo MLM2PRO are the usual picks; around $3,000, camera-based units such as the Bushnell Launch Pro or Uneekor EYE MINI give more accurate indoor club and spin data; premium setups use Foresight, Uneekor overhead or TrackMan systems.

title: Best Caddy towel: Keep Your Clubs Clean & Dry
metaDescription: Find the best caddy towel for your round. Compare materials, clips, and designs to keep your clubs and balls clean on the course.
content:
A reliable caddy towel is an essential accessory for any golfer who wants to keep their clubs, grips, and balls clean throughout the round. Whether you're walking the fairways or riding in a cart, having a dedicated golf towel caddy ensures you're always ready to wipe down your equipment between shots. In this guide, we'll break down the key features to look for, the different types available, and how to choose the best caddy golf towel for your needs.

## Why You Need a Caddy Towel for Golf

Dirt, moisture, and grass clippings can affect your grip and ball spin. A golf caddy towel lets you quickly clean your clubface, remove debris from grooves, and dry your hands or grips. Instead of fumbling with a bulky towel, a caddy towel typically features a clip or carabiner that attaches directly to your bag or belt loop, keeping it within easy reach. Many golfers also use a tour caddy golf towel to wipe down their golf ball before putting. The convenience of a dedicated towel golf accessory can shave strokes by ensuring consistent contact.

## What to Consider Before Buying a Caddy Golf Towel

Before purchasing a caddy golf towel, think about how you'll use it during a round. Here are the main factors to evaluate:

**Size and Thickness**
A standard golf towel caddy is usually around 16x24 inches or smaller. Larger towels offer more surface area for cleaning but can feel bulky when clipped. Thinner microfiber towels dry quickly and pack easily, while thicker terry cloth provides extra absorbency. Choose based on whether you prioritize portability or maximum cleaning power.

**Attachment Mechanism**
Most caddy golf towels come with a metal or plastic clip, a grommet, or a loop. A sturdy clip is crucial if you plan to attach it to your bag, belt, or push cart. Some models feature a carabiner clip that can also be used to hang the towel on a golf cart handle. Check that the clip is corrosion-resistant, especially if you play in humid conditions.

**Material**
Microfiber is the most popular material for modern golf towel caddies. It attracts dust and dirt effectively, dries fast, and won't scratch clubfaces. Cotton or cotton-blend towels offer a classic feel but take longer to dry. If you play in wet weather, a microfiber caddy towel performs better.

Choose a style that reflects your personality or team allegiance, but ensure the practicality isn't compromised.

## Types of Caddy Towels: Material and Design

### Microfiber Caddy Towels
Microfiber is the go-to material for most golfers because it picks up fine particles and wipes away easily. A microfiber caddy golf towel often comes with a loop clip and can be machine washed without losing its effectiveness. They are ideal for cleaning clubs, balls, and even shoes.

### Terry Cloth and Cotton Towels
Traditional terry cloth or cotton towels are soft and highly absorbent. They are often used by golfers who prefer a plush feel for drying hands or wiping sweat. However, they take longer to dry on the course and may leave lint. Some players keep one for general cleaning and a microfiber one for clubfaces.

### Specialty Themed Towels
Themed golf towel caddies add fun to your game. From a camo golf towel for hunters to a caddyshack golf towel that pays homage to the classic movie, these designs are conversation starters. Team-focused options like yankees golf towel, braves towel, uga towel, and usa towel show off your fandom. Novelty designs like frogger golf towel or st andrews golf towel appeal to collectors.

## How to Use and Care for Your Golf Towel Caddy

To get the most out of your caddy towel, keep it attached to your bag or cart where you can access it quickly. After each shot, run the towel over the clubface to remove dirt and grass. For deeper cleaning, dampen the towel slightly with water. At the end of your round, shake off debris and hang the towel to dry.

Wash microfiber towels separately in cold water without fabric softener, as softeners can clog the fibers. Cotton towels can be washed with similar colors. Avoid high heat drying; air dry or use low heat to extend the life of your golf towel caddy.

## FAQ

### What is the difference between a caddy towel and a regular golf towel?
A caddy towel usually includes a built-in clip or grommet for easy attachment to a golf bag or belt. Regular towels lack this feature and are harder to keep accessible during play. Caddy towels are also often smaller and made from quick-drying materials.

### Can I use a caddy golf towel for cleaning my golf glove?
Yes, many golfers find a caddy golf towel useful for drying sweaty hands and grips. Some towels have a designated dry section or a separate loop for this purpose, but any absorbent towel can work. Microfiber towels are particularly good at wicking moisture.

### How often should I replace my golf towel caddy?
Replace your golf towel caddy when you notice it no longer picks up dirt effectively, when it starts to smell despite washing, or if the clip breaks. Quality microfiber models can last several seasons with proper care. Themed towels may be kept longer for decorative use.

## Final Thoughts

Choosing the best caddy towel comes down to your personal preferences for material, attachment style, and design. A good golf towel caddy helps maintain your equipment and keeps your focus on the game. Visit Amazon to browse a wide selection of caddy towel options, and read user reviews to find the one that fits your game perfectly.

title: Best Driver lady: A Complete Guide to Choosing a Women's Golf Driver
metaDescription: Find the best driver lady for your game. Our guide covers key features and what to look for in a women's golf driver.
content:
When it comes to improving your game off the tee, finding the right driver lady is one of the most important equipment decisions a female golfer can make. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned player, a women's driver specifically designed for your swing can add distance, accuracy, and confidence. With so many options available, it helps to understand what sets a woman driver golf apart from unisex or men's models.

## Why Choosing the Right Driver Matters for Women Golfers

Golf drivers for women are engineered differently than standard drivers. They typically feature lighter shafts, higher lofts, and more forgiving clubhead designs. These adjustments help compensate for slower swing speeds often found in female golfers, allowing for better launch conditions and straighter shots. A driver golf women uses may also have a more comfortable grip size and a clubhead shape that inspires confidence at address.

Many female golfers mistakenly think they can use any driver from the rack. However, a womens driver golf club is calibrated for specific swing dynamics. Using a ladies driver golf can make the difference between a slice into the rough and a well-struck shot down the fairway. The right driver also reduces strain, making the game more enjoyable.

## Key Features to Look for in a Women's Golf Driver

When shopping for a golf driver for women, several features should be on your checklist:

**Loft:** Most women's drivers range from 10.5 to 13.5 degrees. Higher lofts help get the ball airborne more easily, which is crucial for slower swing speeds. A higher loft can also reduce sidespin, minimizing slices and hooks.

**Shaft Flex:** Shaft flex is a critical factor. Women's drivers often come with a ladies flex (L) or senior flex (A). These softer shafts allow the club to bend more during the swing, increasing clubhead speed and launch angle. Some golf driver women models also offer a regular flex for stronger players.

**Clubhead Size and Forgiveness:** Modern women's drivers have larger clubheads (440cc to 460cc) with perimeter weighting and high MOI (moment of inertia). This makes them more forgiving on off-center hits, which is especially helpful for recreational golfers. A female golf driver with a draw bias can also help correct a slice.

**Weight:** Weight is a key differentiator. A ladies golf driver is typically lighter overall, often by 10-20 grams compared to a men’s model. This makes it easier to swing and helps generate greater clubhead speed.

**Adjustability:** Some womens golf driver used models offer adjustable loft and lie angles. While not essential, adjustability can help fine-tune ball flight as your swing evolves.

## What to Consider Before Buying a Ladies Golf Driver

Before making a purchase, take stock of your current game. Here are practical points to consider:

**Swing Speed:** Your swing speed dictates the ideal shaft flex and loft. If you don't know your speed, a club fitting at a local shop can provide baseline numbers. Generally, swing speeds below 70 mph benefit from ladies flex and higher lofts.

**Skill Level:** Beginners should prioritize forgiveness over workability. Look for a large sweet spot and perimeter weighting. More advanced players might prefer a driver that allows shot shaping.

**Budget:** Prices for women's drivers vary widely. While new models can be expensive, a womens driver golf used club often performs very similarly to the latest version. Condition matters—check for face wear and shaft integrity.

**Try Before You Buy:** If possible, test a few options at a golf store. Hit them on a launch monitor to see launch angle, spin rate, and carry distance. Many retailers have demo programs.

**Fit Over Brand:** Don't get caught up in brand names. The best driver for you is one that matches your swing characteristics. A well-fitted womens golf driver can outperform a top-tier model that doesn't suit your swing.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Women's Golf Drivers

### What loft is best for a women's golf driver?

Most female golfers benefit from lofts between 11 and 13 degrees. Beginners and those with slower swing speeds often do well with 12 or 13 degrees, while more advanced players may prefer 10.5 or 11. It's best to get fitted or test different lofts.

### Should women use a regular or senior flex shaft in their driver?

Generally, women's drivers come in ladies flex (L), which is softer than senior flex. However, stronger female golfers may use a senior flex or even a regular flex if they swing faster. A club fitting will help determine the right flex for your swing speed.

### Are used women's golf drivers a good option?

Yes, buying a used women's golf driver can be a smart way to get a quality club at a lower price. Look for clean faces, minimal scratches, and a shaft that fits you. Check that the club is not more than a few years old to ensure decent technology.

title: Fastest Golf Cart: The 118 mph Record, and How Fast Normal Carts Go
metaDescription: The fastest golf cart on record hit 118.76 mph. Here's how fast stock, governed, street-legal and modified carts really go, and what it takes (safely) to go faster.
content:
The fastest golf cart on record is **"Bandit"**, built by Plum Quick Motors. It hit **118.76 mph** at Darlington Dragway in South Carolina in 2014 and set the Guinness World Record. It looks like a golf cart, but it was a purpose-built drag machine.

The cart in your garage is a different story. Most golf carts are governed to **12–15 mph**, and street-legal low-speed vehicles top out at **25 mph** by law.

## How fast real carts go

| Type of cart | Typical top speed |
|---|---|
| Course fleet cart | 12–15 mph (often set lower by the course) |
| Personal gas cart, factory | 12–15 mph |
| Gas cart with governor adjusted | ~17 mph on many models |
| Lithium personal cart, sport mode | 18–20 mph on many current models |
| Street-legal LSV | 25 mph maximum (e.g. Club Car Onward LSV) |
| Modified "speed" carts | 25–40+ mph (not road-legal as golf carts) |

## Where extra speed comes from

**Gas carts:** a [governor adjustment](/shop/yamaha-golf-cart-governor-adjustment) is the cheap first step. Beyond that you're looking at clutch springs, gearing or a bigger engine swap.

**Electric carts:** top speed depends on the motor's design RPM, the controller's current limit and the pack voltage. A "high-speed" motor with a matched controller is the usual upgrade. Lithium batteries help because their voltage doesn't sag under load the way lead-acid does. Our [guide to making a cart faster](/blog/how-to-make-a-golf-cart-fast) goes through the options in order of cost.

**Tyres:** taller tyres raise top speed a little and cost you torque. That's why a [lifted cart](/shop/best-golf-cart-lift-kits) on 22-inch tyres can feel slower up hills even when the speedometer shows more on the flat.

## The part speed videos skip

A standard cart has small drum brakes, a short wheelbase, no crumple zones and often no seat belts. At 25 mph it covers more than 36 ft every second. Before you add speed:

- Upgrade to front disc brakes if your model supports them.
- Fit seat belts and keep passengers seated.
- Check steering components and alignment, especially after a lift.
- Know your local rules. A cart doing more than 20 mph on public roads usually has to be a properly equipped and registered [LSV](/shop/best-low-speed-vehicle-golf-cart), not just a fast golf cart.

## Bottom line

118 mph makes a good headline. For your own cart, 17–20 mph with good brakes is the practical sweet spot, and 25 mph belongs on a cart built and registered as an LSV.

faq.answer: The Guinness World Record is 118.76 mph (191 km/h), set in 2014 by Plum Quick Motors' 'Bandit' cart at Darlington Dragway in South Carolina.

faq.question: How fast does a normal golf cart go?
faq.answer: Most fleet and personal golf carts are governed to about 12–15 mph. Street-legal low-speed vehicles (LSVs) are capped at 25 mph.

faq.question: How can I make my golf cart faster?
faq.answer: On gas carts, a governor adjustment usually adds a few mph. On electric carts, a higher-speed motor and matching controller, or a lithium pack that holds voltage, make the biggest difference. Bigger tyres raise top speed slightly but cost torque. Upgrade brakes before you add speed.

faq.question: Are lifted golf carts faster?
faq.answer: Slightly, if they run taller tyres, since each wheel revolution covers more ground. But acceleration, hill climbing and braking get worse, and the higher centre of gravity makes fast corners riskier.

title: Best Golf Cart Engine Conversion Kit – Upgrade Your Ride
metaDescription: Discover top golf cart engine conversion kits for gas, electric, AC, turbo, and 4x4 builds. Expert tips on choosing the right kit for your cart.
content:
If you're looking to breathe new life into your golf cart, a golf cart engine conversion kit can transform its performance, efficiency, and fun factor. Whether you want more speed, better torque, or the ability to tackle rough terrain, choosing the right conversion kit is essential. This article explores the types of kits available, what to consider before buying, and key features to look for.

## Why Convert Your Golf Cart Engine?

Golf carts are versatile vehicles, but their stock engines often leave room for improvement. Converting your engine can:

- **Increase speed and power** – Upgrading from a standard motor to a high-torque or turbo setup gives you more thrill on and off the course.
- **Improve efficiency** – Electric conversions can reduce operational costs and maintenance.
- **Enable off-road capability** – 4wd golf cart conversion kits or golf cart 4x4 conversion kits let you explore trails and rough terrain.
- **Extend battery life** – For electric carts, a 48v golf cart conversion kit can significantly boost range.

Whether you want a quiet, emission-free ride with an electric golf cart conversion kit or the raw power of a gas upgrade, there’s a solution for every need.

## Types of Golf Cart Engine Conversion Kits

Golf cart engine conversion kits come in several varieties. Understanding the differences helps you match the kit to your goals:

### Gas Conversion Kits
These replace or upgrade the existing gas engine for more horsepower and torque. They’re popular for off-road builds and heavy-duty use. Some kits include a golf cart turbo kit to force more air into the engine, boosting performance significantly.

### Electric Conversion Kits
Electric golf cart conversion kits swap out the gas engine for an electric motor and battery pack. They offer quiet operation, zero emissions, and lower running costs. A 48v golf cart conversion kit is common for balancing speed and range, while a golf cart ac conversion kit provides smoother acceleration and regenerative braking.

### AC Conversion Kits
AC (alternating current) systems are more efficient than DC motors. An ac golf cart conversion kit typically delivers better torque and longer battery life, making it a favorite among serious enthusiasts.

### 4×4 and Off-Road Kits
For those who venture beyond the fairway, 4wd golf cart conversion kits or golf cart 4x4 conversion kits include lift kits, heavy-duty axles, and upgraded drivetrains. These are often paired with gas or high-torque electric motors.

### Push Cart Conversion Kits
Golf push cart conversion kits are a niche option for converting a manual push cart into a powered caddy. They’re light, compact, and easy to install.

## What to Consider Before Buying a Golf Cart Engine Conversion Kit

Before you purchase a golf cart engine conversion kit, evaluate these factors to avoid costly mistakes:

- **Compatibility** – Check your cart’s make, model, and year. Kits are often specific to brands like EZGO, Club Car, or Yamaha.
- **Skill Level** – Some kits are plug-and-play; others require welding, electrical work, or mechanical expertise. Be honest about your DIY ability.
- **Goal** – Define your primary use: cruising, towing, off-roading, or racing. This dictates the type (gas vs. electric, AC vs. DC, 2WD vs. 4WD).
- **Local Regulations** – Some areas have restrictions on modified golf carts (speed limits, noise, street legality). Check with your local DMV or club.
- **Budget** – Costs vary widely. While we don’t list specific prices, factor in the kit, installation, and potential upgrades like batteries or controllers.
- **Warranty and Support** – Look for sellers that offer technical support and a reasonable warranty on the kit components.

## Top Features to Look for in a Conversion Kit

When comparing golf cart conversion kits, prioritize these features:

- **Motor Power** – Measured in horsepower (HP) or kilowatts (kW). For electric kits, voltage (36V, 48V, 72V) and amp-hour (Ah) ratings indicate potential performance.
- **Controller Quality** – A good controller manages power delivery smoothly. For AC systems, ensure it supports regenerative braking.
- **Ease of Installation** – Kits with detailed manuals, pre-wired harnesses, and all necessary hardware save time and frustration.
- **Durability** – Look for sealed motors and corrosion-resistant components if you drive in wet conditions.
- **Upgrade Path** – Some kits allow future enhancements like battery upgrades or turbo add-ons.
- **Brand Reputation** – Stick with known manufacturers that have positive reviews from the golf cart community.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I install a golf cart engine conversion kit myself?
Yes, many DIY enthusiasts install their own kits. Basic mechanical and electrical skills are required. For complex gas or AC conversions, you may need help from a professional mechanic. Always follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

### What is the difference between a gas and electric golf cart conversion kit?
Gas kits offer raw power and quick refueling, but produce noise and fumes. Electric kits are quieter, cleaner, and have lower operating costs, but require battery charging and have a limited range per charge. AC electric kits provide better efficiency than DC.

### Will a conversion kit affect the resale value of my golf cart?
It can go either way. A professional, desirable conversion (like a quality AC or turbo gas kit) may increase value for the right buyer. Poorly installed or excessive modifications could decrease it. Keep records and receipts to demonstrate quality.

In summary, a kit is a smart investment if you want to personalize your ride. By understanding the types, considering your needs, and choosing quality components, you can enjoy a cart that performs exactly how you want. Whether you upgrade to a 48v golf cart conversion kit, drop in a golf cart turbo kit, or go all-in with a 4x4 conversion, the aftermarket has you covered. Happy driving!

title: Best Golf Knit Headcovers
metaDescription: Discover the best golf knit headcovers for protecting your woods and hybrids. What to consider before buying, popular types, and care tips.
content:
Golf knit headcovers have become a popular choice for players who want to add a touch of personality to their bag while protecting their clubs. Unlike standard neoprene or leather covers, knit headcovers offer a classic, handcrafted look that stands out on the course. Whether you're looking for a set of knitted golf headcovers for your driver, fairway woods, or hybrids, this guide will help you find the right options without the fluff.

## Why Golfers Are Switching to Knit Headcovers

Knit headcovers provide more than just aesthetics. The thick, stretchy yarn helps cushion clubheads against bumps and scratches during transport. Many golfers appreciate that a golf knit headcover option fits snugly without slipping off, even when walking the course. Additionally, the breathable material allows moisture to escape, reducing the chance of rust on metal clubs. For those who enjoy a retro or handmade vibe, a set of stitch golf headcovers can also double as a conversation starter in the clubhouse.

## What to Consider Before Buying Knit Headcovers

Before you add knit golf headcovers to your bag, think about these factors:

**Fit and Size** – Headcovers come in different sizes for drivers, fairway woods, and hybrids. Some manufactures offer one-size-fits-most designs, but check if the cover is deep enough to cover the entire clubhead. A loose cover may fall off; a too-tight one could be hard to remove.

**Yarn Quality and Durability** – Look for thick, tightly knitted yarn that won't pill or stretch out after a few rounds. Blends with acrylic or cotton tend to hold their shape better than pure wool.

**Closure and Retention** – Some knit headcovers have a pom-pom or tassel to help keep them in place, while others rely on a tight knit. If you carry your bag or use a cart, a cover with a secure fit is essential.

**Design and Personal Style** – From solid colors to animal motifs or team logos, the best knit golf headcovers let you express your personality. Consider whether you want a matching set or mix-and-match patterns.

**Weather Resistance** – Knit covers are not waterproof, but some are treated with a light DWR (durable water repellent) coating. If you often play in damp conditions, look for options that resist moisture.

## Popular Varieties of Knitted Golf Headcovers

When browsing options, you'll find several popular types:

**Classic Cable Knit** – Inspired by traditional sweaters, cable knit golf head covers offer a timeless look. They are usually thicker and provide extra padding.

**Fair Isle Patterns** – These multicolored geometric designs add a Scottish flair to your bag. They pair well with a vintage-style leather golf bag.

**Character or Novelty Knits** – Some companies produce stitch golf headcovers shaped like animals, sports equipment, or humorous objects. These are great for casual rounds or as gifts.

**Custom or Personalized** – Many knitters on marketplaces like Amazon offer custom knit hybrid golf head covers with your initials, favorite team, or a unique color scheme.

**Matching Sets** – If you want a uniform look, complete sets for driver, fairway woods, and hybrids are often sold together. These reduce the hassle of coordinating separate items.

## Tips for Choosing the Right Knit Headcover for Your Game

1. **Consider Your Club Length** – Drivers and fairway woods have different shaft lengths and head sizes. Make sure the cover you choose is designed for the specific club type.
2. **Check the Opening** – A wide, elasticized opening makes it easier to slide the cover on and off. Some designs have a drawstring to tighten the opening.
3. **Evaluate the Lining** – Some knit headcovers have a soft fleece or plush lining inside to prevent scratching. This is especially important for delicate finishes.
4. **Look at Reviews** – Read what other golfers say about how the cover holds up after months of use. Look for comments about fading, pilling, or stretching.
5. **Balance Style and Utility** – While a flashy cover looks great, it should also do its job. Avoid covers with long tassels or loose parts that could catch on your bag or cart.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Knit Golf Headcovers

**Q: Are knit headcovers better than neoprene?**
A: Knit headcovers offer more style and breathability, but neoprene provides better water resistance and impact protection. The choice depends on your priorities: looks and comfort vs. maximum protection.

**Q: How do I clean my knitted golf head covers?**
A: Most knit headcovers can be hand washed in cold water with mild detergent and laid flat to dry. Avoid machine washing or drying, as that can cause shrinking or stretching.

**Q: Can I use a knit headcover on a putter?**
A: Yes, but putter headcovers are typically smaller. Look for specifically designed knit putter covers, or a mini-sized pattern. Standard driver covers will be too large.

Choosing the right golf knit headcovers can enhance both the protection and personality of your clubs. By focusing on fit, material, and your personal style, you can find a set that keeps your equipment safe and makes you smile every time you pull a club. title: Best Waterproof Golf Bag: Keep Your Gear Dry in Any Weather
metaDescription: Find the best waterproof golf bag for your game. Compare stand bags, cart bags, and covers. Expert tips on what to look for before buying.
content:
Rain can turn a perfect round into a frustrating experience—especially when your clubs, clothes, and electronics get soaked. A waterproof golf bag is more than a luxury; it’s essential gear for golfers who play in unpredictable weather. Whether you walk the course with a stand bag or ride in a cart, keeping your equipment dry protects your investment and keeps you focused on the game. In this guide, we break down what to look for, the different types available, and how to choose the right bag for your needs.

## What to Consider Before Buying a Waterproof Golf Bag

Before you shop for a waterproof golf bag solution, think about your typical playing conditions and how you carry your gear. Not all waterproof bags are created equal, and the right choice depends on several factors:

- **Waterproof vs. Water Resistant**: True waterproof bags use sealed seams, waterproof zippers, and coated fabrics to prevent water ingress. Water resistant golf bags repel light rain but may leak in heavy downpours. For full protection, look for bags with an IP rating or manufacturer claims of 100% waterproof construction.
- **Weight and Portability**: If you walk the course, a lightest waterproof golf bag is a priority. Best lightweight waterproof golf bag options use advanced materials like nylon or TPU to shed weight without sacrificing durability. However, lighter bags may have fewer pockets or less padding.
- **Storage and Organization**: Look for enough pockets for your essentials—rain gloves, extra balls, rangefinder, and waterproof golf apparel. A dedicated waterproof valuables pocket is a plus. Also consider the number of dividers; full-length dividers prevent club tangle.
- **Durability and Warranty**: Check the fabric denier and seam construction. Brands like **Sun Mountain** offer golf bag sun mountain waterproof models known for ruggedness. A longer warranty often indicates confidence in waterproofing.

## Types of Waterproof Golf Bags

Waterproof golf bags come in several styles to match different playing habits:

### Waterproof Stand Bags
These are the most popular for walkers. A waterproof golf stand bag features a built-in stand mechanism that keeps the bag upright on the course. Look for models with waterproof zippers and sealed seams. Many top manufacturers produce taylormade waterproof golf stand bag options, but other brands also offer competitive designs. Stand bags are generally lighter but may have less storage than cart bags.

### Waterproof Cart Bags
Designed for riders, these bags are larger and heavier, fitting securely on a golf cart. They often have more pockets, including insulated cooler pockets and apparel compartments. A cart bag paired with a golf cart waterproof cover can provide double protection in heavy rain. However, they lack a stand, so they are less convenient for walking.

### Waterproof Bag Covers
If you already own a non-waterproof bag, a bag cover is a cost-effective solution. These slip over your entire bag and cinch tight to seal out moisture. They are great for rain delays or storing your bag in wet conditions. Some covers are padded for extra protection during travel.

## Key Features to Look For

When evaluating best waterproof golf bags, focus on these critical features:

- **Waterproof Zippers**: Traditional zippers leak even if the fabric is waterproof. Look for bags with waterproof zippers (often called AquaGuard or similar). They have a rubber coating or tape that seals the teeth.
- **Sealed Seams**: Seams are the weakest point. High-quality bags use taped or welded seams, much like a rain jacket.
- **Waterproof Materials**: Common materials include PVC, TPU, and coated nylon. TPU is lightweight and flexible, while PVC is more durable but heavier.
- **Drainage**: Some bags have drain holes in the bottom to let out any water that seeps in, preventing your clubs from sitting in water.
- **Rain Hood Included**: Many waterproof bags come with a matching rain hood for extra head covering.

## Top Waterproof Golf Bag Options

While specific models change yearly, the best waterproof golf bags consistently come from brands like Sun Mountain, TaylorMade, Callaway, and Ping. Look for best waterproof golf bags in the following categories:

- **Best Overall**: A well-balanced bag with full waterproofing, ample storage, and good organization. Often a mid-weight stand bag with 14-way dividers.
- **Best Lightweight**: The lightest waterproof golf bag options weigh under 5 pounds. Ideal for walkers who want maximum portability without sacrificing rain protection.
- **Best Value**: Bags that offer solid waterproofing at a lower price point. These might use water-resistant materials with a rain cover rather than fully waterproof construction.
- **Best for Cart Use**: Large cart bags with multiple pockets and easy-access panels. Pair with a water resistant golf bags cover if you play in heavy rain.

Remember that no bag is 100% waterproof forever—zippers and seams can wear over time. Regular maintenance and proper storage extend the life of your water proof golf bag.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the difference between water resistant and waterproof golf bags?
Water resistant bags repel light moisture but will eventually let water through in heavy rain or when submerged. Waterproof golf bags use sealed seams, waterproof zippers, and coated fabrics to stop water completely. For full protection, choose a bag labeled as waterproof rather than water resistant.

### Can I use a waterproof golf bag cover on any bag?
Yes, a bag cover fits most standard golf bags. It slips over your bag and cinches at the bottom to seal out rain. This is a practical solution if you already own a non-waterproof bag, but it adds extra weight and may not be as convenient as a built-in waterproof design.

### How do I maintain my waterproof golf bag?
To prolong the life of your best lightweight waterproof golf bag, rinse off dirt and saltwater after use. Check zippers and seams for wear periodically. Store the bag in a dry place. Some bags allow reproofing with a spray-on waterproofing treatment, but always follow the manufacturer’s instructions. Avoid overstuffing pockets, as that can stress seams.

## Final Thoughts

Investing in a quality bag ensures your clubs, electronics, and dry layers stay protected round after round. Whether you prefer a waterproof golf stand bag for walking or a cart bag with extra storage, focus on true waterproof construction over water resistance. Pair your bag clothes for complete confidence on rainy days. Check the latest models from trusted brands and read reviews to find the bag that matches your game.

title: Which Hand Do You Wear a Golf Glove On?
metaDescription: You wear a golf glove on your lead hand: the left hand for right-handed golfers, the right hand for left-handers. Why, when to wear two, when to take it off, and how it should fit.
content:
You wear a golf glove on your **lead hand**, the one at the top of the grip. For a **right-handed golfer that's the left hand**, and for a **left-handed golfer it's the right hand**. When you shop, "left-hand glove" means a glove worn *on* the left hand, which is the one right-handed players buy.

## Why the lead hand

Your lead hand holds the top of the club and controls the clubface. Most of the grip pressure, and most of the slipping, happens there, especially in heat, humidity or rain. A glove gives you a consistent tacky surface and stops blisters on the heel pad and fingers. The trail hand is usually left bare so you can feel the club.

## Two gloves, no glove

- **Two gloves:** perfectly legal and common in rain, cold weather, or for golfers with sensitive skin or arthritis. Rain gloves are often sold in pairs and grip better when wet.
- **No glove:** some good players never wear one. If your grips are in good condition and you don't blister, it's your choice.
- **Putting:** most golfers take the glove off to putt and for delicate chips, to get more feel.

## Getting the fit right

1. **Snug, not tight.** There should be no loose leather at the fingertips or across the palm.
2. **The tab should fasten about three-quarters across.** If it overlaps fully, the glove is too big. If it barely reaches, it's too small.
3. **Regular vs cadet.** Cadet sizes have shorter fingers and a wider palm. If regular gloves always leave spare material at your fingertips, try cadet. Our [cadet vs regular guide](/shop/cadet-vs-regular-golf-glove) explains it.
4. **Leather vs synthetic.** Cabretta leather feels best but wears faster. Synthetic and hybrid gloves last longer and handle sweat better.

## Make it last

- Take it off between shots on hot days and fasten it to your bag.
- Flatten it after the round and keep it in its packet or a glove holder so it doesn't dry out stiff.
- Rotate two gloves during a round in the heat.
- Carry a spare. It's on our [golf bag checklist](/shop/golf-bag-checklist) for a reason.

A glove that wears through quickly at the heel pad can be a sign of a grip held too much in the palm, or grips that need replacing.

title: Best 2 Piece Golf Balls: Top Picks for Distance and Durability
metaDescription: Looking for the best 2 piece golf balls? Read our guide on two piece golf balls, their benefits, and what to consider before buying.
content:
If you're looking for golf balls that deliver maximum distance and durability without breaking the bank, 2 piece golf balls are your best bet. These balls are the most popular choice among beginners, high handicappers, and even some mid-level players who prioritize straighter flight and long carries. In this guide, we'll break down everything you need to know about two piece golf balls, from construction to buying considerations, and highlight some top options on the market.

## What Are 2 Piece Golf Balls?

Two piece golf balls have the simplest construction: a solid rubber core surrounded by a durable cover (usually Surlyn or ionomer). Unlike multi-layer balls (3, 4, or 5 piece), the 2 piece design minimizes spin and maximizes energy transfer at impact. This results in higher ball speeds, lower spin rates, and longer distances—especially for golfers with moderate swing speeds. Common examples include the Titleist DT TruSoft, TaylorMade Rocketballz, and Callaway Supersoft.

## Benefits of Using Two Piece Golf Balls

- **Distance**: The low-spin design helps reduce slice or hook, keeping shots straighter and longer.
- **Durability**: The tough cover resists scuffs and cuts better than softer urethane covers, making them last dozens of rounds.
- **Affordability**: Two piece balls are generally cheaper than multi-layer premium balls, great for budget-conscious golfers.
- **Low Compression**: Many two piece balls have low compression (e.g., 40-60), ideal for slower swing speeds (< 85 mph) to achieve better feel and distance.

## What to Consider Before Buying 2 Piece Golf Balls

Before you buy a box of two piece golf balls, keep these factors in mind:

- **Compression**: Lower compression balls (e.g., 50) are softer and help slower swingers get more distance. Higher compression balls (e.g., 80) suit faster swings. Most two piece balls are low-to-mid compression.
- **Cover Material**: Surlyn covers are durable and provide a firm feel. Ionomer covers offer a slightly softer feel and more greenside spin. For pure distance, Surlyn is common.
- **Brand and Price**: Stick with reputable brands like Titleist, TaylorMade, Callaway, Srixon, or Wilson. Two piece balls range from budget to mid-price; avoid unknown knockoffs.
- **Color Options**: Some two piece golf balls come in **two toned** or **two color** designs (e.g., half white/half yellow) for better visibility. Also available in matte finishes.
- **Your Skill Level**: Beginners and high handicappers (shooting 100+) benefit most from 2 piece balls. Intermediate players may prefer 3 piece for more spin control.

## Best 2 Piece Golf Balls on the Market

While we don't rank one as the absolute best (personal preference varies), here are some consistently popular 2 piece golf balls that deliver solid performance:

- **Titleist DT TruSoft**: A low-compression (60) ball with a soft feel and good distance. Often considered one of the best 2 piece golf balls for feel.
- **TaylorMade Rocketballz**: Known for explosive distance and a durable Surlyn cover. Great value.
- **Callaway Supersoft**: Ultra-low compression (38) for maximum distance with slow swings. Very soft feel.
- **Srixon Soft Feel**: Low compression with a soft cover that provides decent greenside control for a two piece ball.
- **Wilson Staff Duo**: Offers a very low compression (29) for players with slow swing speeds.

For a full 2 piece golf balls list, you can search on Amazon using the link below to see current prices and reviews.

## 2 Piece vs 3 Piece Golf Balls

If you're comparing 2 vs 3 piece golf balls, here's the quick difference:

- **2 piece**: Longer, straighter, more durable, less spin. Best for beginners, high handicappers, or budget players.
- **3 piece**: A layer between core and cover adds spin control and feel around the greens. Better for intermediate and advanced players who want to shape shots.

Most weekend golfers will score lower with 2 piece balls due to reduced slices and hooks. Only consider switching when you consistently break 90.

## FAQ

### Are 2 piece golf balls good for beginners?

Yes, absolutely. Two piece golf balls are ideal for beginners because they reduce side spin, which means fewer slices and hooks. They also fly farther with less effort and are more forgiving on mishits. Plus, they're durable and affordable, so you won't mind losing a few in the woods.

### Do pros use 2 piece golf balls?

Most tour professionals use 3, 4, or 5 piece balls to maximize spin control around the greens. However, some long-drive competitors and club pros may use 2 piece balls for max distance. For the average golfer, a 2 piece ball is more than sufficient.

### What is the difference between 2 piece and 3 piece golf balls?

The main difference is construction and performance. A 2 piece ball has one core and one cover, producing low spin and high distance. A 3 piece ball adds an intermediate layer, increasing spin and control on approach shots and around the green. Two piece balls are better for distance and durability; three piece balls offer more feel and workability.

## Final Thoughts

Choosing the right golf ball can lower your scores instantly. For most recreational golfers, two piece golf balls provide the best combination of distance, durability, and value. Start with a low-compression model if you have a slow swing, and don't be afraid to experiment with different brands. Check out the recommended link for current deals on 2 piece golf balls.

title: 2022 E-Z-GO Golf Carts: Models, Used Prices and What to Check Before Buying
metaDescription: Buying a 2022 E-Z-GO? The model-year line-up (Liberty, Freedom RXV and TXT, Express, ELiTE lithium), what a 4-year-old cart is worth, how to confirm the year and a used-cart checklist.
content:
A 2022 E-Z-GO is now about four years old. That's often a sweet spot for used buyers: modern features, plenty of life left and a price well below new. Used E-Z-GOs typically keep **about 55–70% of their new price at 3–5 years old**, so expect most 2022 carts to sell for **roughly two-thirds of what they cost new**. Battery type and condition explain most of the difference between two carts that look the same.

## The 2022 E-Z-GO line-up

| Model | Seats | What it is | Power options |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Freedom TXT** | 2 | The classic, simple two-seater | Electric (lead-acid or lithium), gas |
| **Freedom RXV** | 2 | Newer chassis, AC drive, smoother ride | Electric (incl. ELiTE lithium), gas |
| **Liberty** | 4 | All forward-facing seats, compact footprint | ELiTE lithium |
| **Express S4 / S6 / L6** | 4–6 | Personal transport and utility, some lifted | Electric and gas |
| **Street-legal (LSV) versions** | 2–6 | Lights, belts, VIN, 25 mph | Electric |

"ELiTE" is E-Z-GO's lithium battery system. On a used cart, the battery is the single biggest value factor.

## Confirm the year first

Body panels, seats and roofs get swapped all the time, so the look of a cart tells you little. Read the **serial number plate** and decode it. Our guide on [how to tell what year an EZGO is](/blog/how-to-tell-what-year-a-ezgo-golf-cart-is) shows where to find it and how to read it. If the plate is missing or damaged, walk away or negotiate hard.

## What a 2022 is worth

| Age | Typical share of new price |
|---|---|
| 1–2 years | 75–85% |
| 3–5 years (a 2022 today) | **55–70%** |
| 6–8 years | 35–50% |
| 9+ years | 20–35% |

Recent new prices for comparison: TXT about $9,500–$12,500, RXV $11,500–$14,500, Liberty $12,500–$16,500, plus freight. Lithium adds roughly $2,000–$3,500 new, and a healthy lithium pack holds that value much better than a tired lead-acid set. Our [used E-Z-GO value guide](/shop/used-ezgo-golf-cart-value) goes deeper.

## Used 2022 checklist

1. **Battery.** For lithium, ask for the install date, any warranty and the charger model. For lead-acid, check the date codes and do a [battery health test](/blog/how-to-tell-if-a-golf-cart-battery-is-bad). A lead-acid pack near the end of its life is a $1,000+ negotiation point.
2. **Test drive.** Check the hill climb, the brakes (straight stops, no grinding) and the steering (no wander or clunks), and make sure forward and reverse work smoothly.
3. **Charger.** It should match the pack. Lithium needs a lithium-compatible charger.
4. **Frame and underside.** Look for rust or corrosion around the battery tray on lead-acid carts, and cracked suspension mounts on lifted ones.
5. **Modifications.** Lift kits, bigger tyres and speed upgrades are fine if done well, but ask for receipts.
6. **Paperwork.** For LSVs, check the title and registration. For any cart, a bill of sale that includes the serial number.

## Bottom line

A 2022 E-Z-GO with a healthy lithium pack is one of the safer used-cart buys. Expect to pay around two-thirds of new. Check the serial number, test the battery, and let the battery's condition, not the paint or wheels, decide your offer.

In this guide, we’ll help you navigate the options and find the best golf bags for women based on your playing style.

## What to Consider Before Buying a Women’s Golf Bag

Before you pick a bag, think about how you play. Four key factors will influence your choice:

- **Weight**: If you walk and carry your bag, lightweight models (under 4–5 lbs) are essential. Cart bags can be heavier but often come with more features.
- **Storage**: How many clubs do you carry? Full sets (14 clubs) need enough slots. Also consider pockets for accessories, valuables, and hydration.
- **Stand vs. Cart**: Stand bags are great for walkers because they have retractable legs that keep the bag upright. Cart bags are designed to sit securely on a golf cart and often have more organized storage.
- **Style & Design**: Many women want a bag that looks good. There are plenty of cool womens golf bags and trendy womens golf bags that combine function with fashion. Designer golf bags for women are also available if you want a premium look.

## Best Golf Bags for Women by Use Case

### Lightweight Stand Bags for Walkers

If you prefer walking the course, a lightweight stand bag is your best bet. These bags typically weigh around 4–5 pounds and have comfortable dual straps for even weight distribution. Look for a golf bag for ladies that includes a stand that deploys easily. Popular options feature 4–6 pockets, a rain hood, and a padded hip pad. For extra convenience, some have a cooler pocket or range finder holder. Many of these are considered the best ladies golf bag for active players.

### Cart Bags for Maximum Organization

For riders or those who use a push cart, a cart bag offers superior storage and stability. These are often heavier but have more club dividers (often 14-way tops) to prevent tangling. They also have large pockets for extra clothing, shoes, and accessories. If you carry a full set and want everything organized, a cart bag is a solid choice. Some are designed with a pass-through for cart straps, making them easy to secure. Shop for best ladies golf bags in this category if you value space over weight.

### Stylish & Trendy Bags for the Fashion-Conscious

title: Best Electric Golf Cart Speed Limiter
metaDescription: Discover the best electric golf cart speed limiter for safety and compliance. Learn how to control speed, what to consider before buying, and FAQs.
content:
If you own an electric golf cart, managing its speed is crucial for safety, battery life, and compliance with course or road regulations. An electric golf cart speed limiter is the most effective tool to cap your cart’s top speed, ensuring it stays within safe limits. Whether you’re looking to reduce speed for younger drivers, adhere to community rules, or simply prevent accidental high-speed surges, this guide covers everything you need to know about electric golf cart speed limiters—how they work, what to consider before buying, and answers to common questions.

## Understanding Electric Golf Cart Speed Limiters

An electric golf cart speed limiter is a device that restricts the maximum speed of your cart by controlling the power delivered to the motor. It works in conjunction with the electric golf cart speed controller, which governs acceleration and overall performance. Without a limiter, many electric carts can reach speeds of 15–25 mph or more, depending on the model and modifications. A speed limiter ensures the cart stays at a predetermined safe speed, often adjustable from 12 to 19 mph. This is especially important if your golf course or homeowners association enforces strict speed limits.

## How Does a Speed Limiter Work?

Most modern electric golf carts use a programmable speed controller that receives signals from the throttle and governor. A speed limiter can be a simple mechanical adapter that restricts throttle movement or an electronic module that limits voltage or current to the motor. Electronic limiters are more precise and often plug-and-play. When installed, they override the controller’s settings to cap the electric golf cart top speed at a user-defined value. Some advanced models allow you to set multiple speed profiles, such as one for course use and another for neighborhood driving.

## Key Benefits of Installing a Speed Limiter

- **Safety**: Prevents the cart from exceeding safe speeds, reducing the risk of accidents, especially for inexperienced drivers or children.
- **Battery Conservation**: Limiting speed can extend battery range and lifespan by reducing power draw during acceleration.
- **Legal Compliance**: Many golf courses, resorts, and residential communities require carts to stay under a certain speed. A limiter helps you avoid fines or being banned from the course.
- **Insurance Savings**: Some insurers offer discounts for carts equipped with speed limiters, as they lower liability.

## What to Consider Before Buying a Speed Limiter

When shopping for an limiter, keep these factors in mind:

1. **Compatibility with Your Cart Model**: Speed limiters are often designed for specific brands like EZGO, Club Car, Yamaha, or Yamaha Drive. Check the product description to ensure it fits your cart’s year and model. For example, an EZGO electric golf cart speed adjustment TXT may require a different limiter than a newer RXV.
2. **Installation Difficulty**: Some limiters are plug-and-play, while others require splicing wires. If you’re not comfortable with electrical work, look for a model with simple instructions or professional installation options.
3. **Adjustability**: Choose a limiter that lets you set the top speed to multiple levels (e.g., 12, 15, 19 mph). Fixed limiters are cheaper but less flexible.
4. **Durability and Weather Resistance**: Golf carts are used outdoors, so ensure the limiter is waterproof and built to withstand vibration and temperature changes.
5. **Warranty and Support**: Although we avoid mentioning specific brands, look for a limiter that offers at least a one-year warranty and responsive customer service.
6. **User Reviews**: Check real-world feedback on platforms like Amazon to see if others successfully used it on their electric golf cart speed setup.

## Installation Tips and Considerations

Installing a speed limiter is generally straightforward, but follow these tips:

- Always disconnect the battery before starting.
- Locate your cart’s speed controller (usually under the seat or behind the dash). The limiter will either plug into a harness or connect to specific wires.
- If the instructions are unclear, search for a video tutorial for your specific cart model.
- After installation, test the cart in a safe, open area to confirm the speed is capped as desired. If the limiter is adjustable, start with the lowest setting and increase gradually.
- Remember that removing or bypassing a speed limiter may void the cart’s warranty or violate local laws. Only use it as intended.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I remove the speed limiter on my electric golf cart?

Yes, many speed limiters can be removed or disabled, but doing so may allow the cart to reach its full potential speed. However, if you want to remove speed limiter on electric golf cart, be aware that this could lead to safety risks, battery drain, and legal issues on courses or streets that require speed caps. Always check local regulations before removal.

### How fast will my golf cart go with a speed limiter?

This depends on the limiter’s setting and your cart’s base speed. Most limiters allow you to choose a top speed between 12 and 19 mph. For example, a typical electric golf cart might go 15 mph with a limiter set to that speed. Some adjustable models let you go as low as 8 mph for very controlled environments.

### Are electric golf cart speed limiters legal?

Yes, speed limiters are generally legal, but they must comply with local traffic laws. Many states limit golf carts on public roads to 20 mph or less. A limiter ensures your cart stays within that limit. However, how fast can an electric golf cart go without a limiter—often 25 mph or more—may be illegal on certain roads. Always verify your area’s regulations.

## Final Thoughts

An limiter is a simple, affordable upgrade that enhances safety, extends battery life, and keeps you on the right side of course or road rules. When choosing one, prioritize compatibility, adjustability, and ease of installation. While you can find various options on Amazon, read product details carefully to match your cart’s make and model. By capping your cart’s speed, you’ll enjoy worry-free cruising whether on the fairway or through the neighborhood.

Remember: Always prioritize safety and follow manufacturer guidelines for installation and use.
